channel.title: HSJ - Latest news
channel.description: Custom RSS feed for HSJ latest news

item.title: Mentally ill men forced into prison to get a bed
item.description: Police are sending people in mental health crisis to prison when they should be in a secure hospital, with “devastating consequences”, inspectors have warned.

item.title: Patient safety brief upgraded in new DHSC team
item.description: Patient safety and public health have been upgraded to a ministerial responsibility, the Department of Health and Social Care has announced.

item.title: Strikes at two hospitals extended
item.description: A fresh round of strikes set to last 20 days has been announced at hospitals in Lancashire in a row over holiday pay.

item.title: Lack of doctors closes maternity unit
item.description: A rural maternity unit is closing this week, despite local opposition, blaming a lack of doctors.

item.title: Candidates for £342k DHSC job to face mock PAC
item.description: Candidates for a readvertised post in the Department of Health and Social Care’s executive team, with pay up to £342,000, have been advised to expect a mock public accounts committee grilling.

item.title: Trust identifies ‘power imbalances’ after sexual misconduct sackings
item.description: An ambulance trust is to strengthen safeguarding for students after sacking two senior staff for sexual misconduct and identifying “inherent power imbalances” that put learners at risk.

item.title: Probe into hospital AI safety launched
item.description: AI tools that are already being rolled out across the NHS face an investigation by the national safety body.

item.title: 159 sites to get £343m for ‘A&Es’ and health centres
item.description: The government has named the 159 provisional sites for new mental health emergency departments and community centres, which will share £343m of capital.

item.title: Regions roll out custom performance regimes
item.description: NHS England regions have begun introducing their own regional performance management regimes for providers, on top of the NHS Oversight Framework.

item.title: CEOs agree new targets to cut waits
item.description: A new set of targets has been agreed between NHS England and mental health chief executives in a bid to boost the sector’s reputation within government.

item.title: Threat to remove resident doctors after racist incidents
item.description: One of England’s most challenged trusts faces resident doctors being removed from two specialties due to racism from staff and patients, board papers have revealed.

item.title: Council privatises NHS-run care service
item.description: Private providers are set to take over the running of some adult social care services currently carried out by an NHS trust in the South West.

item.title: Shared execs may be ‘stretched and less effective’, NHSE admits
item.description: Sharing executives across struggling providers can lead to leadership teams becoming “stretched and therefore less effective”, NHS England has acknowledged.

item.title: Lead provider role creating ‘potential conflicts of interest’, review finds
item.description: A lack of clarity around lead provider and commissioner roles at a mental health trust collaborative is creating “potential conflicts of interest”, a review has found.

item.title: Exclusive: Blindsided NHSE bosses to launch snooping probe
item.description: Blindsided NHS England bosses have ordered a “thorough investigation” into the trust at the centre of a scandal involving staff inappropriately accessing patients’ records, HSJ can reveal.

item.title: Trusts failed to act on 9,000 lost patients for five years
item.description: Clinicians and managers knew of problems with an ear, nose, and throat waiting list five years before a backlog of nearly 9,000 patients came to light, an NHS England review has found.

item.title: Director unfairly sacked by CEO after ‘17 years unblemished service’
item.description: A former trust CEO “misled” one of his board executives who was sacked after a “deeply flawed” investigation, an employment tribunal has found.

item.title: ICBs told to redraw boundaries again
item.description: Integrated care board boundaries will be redrawn again after Andy Burnham pledged they would match new local government footprints by 2029.

item.title: Welsh government denies English hospital’s £20m demand
item.description: A Welsh health board is refusing to pay £21m as demanded by an English hospital trust in a cross-border funding dispute.

item.title: ‘Nepotistic culture’ left poor behaviour unchecked, says review
item.description: Staff at a major acute trust described a “nepotistic culture” in which poor behaviour went unpunished, a review into how it handled staff concerns has found.
